paragraphs.title: The Request for Guidance and the People's Commitment

answers: Jeremiah the prophet
The king of Babylon
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: The people came to Jeremiah and asked him to pray unto the Lord for them.
easy.q: To whom did the people bring their request?

answers: Build them a city
Pray for them and ask for guidance
Lead them into Egypt
easy.explanation: They asked Jeremiah to pray and learn the way they should walk and the thing they should do.
easy.q: What did the people ask Jeremiah to do?

answers: Obey the voice of the Lord
Fight against the king of Babylon
Remain forever in Jerusalem
easy.explanation: They promised to obey the Lord whether His answer was good or evil.
easy.q: What did the people promise to do after hearing the Lord's answer?

answers: To describe their small number after the destruction
To say that they had a large army
To announce that they were leaving the land
medium.explanation: They described themselves as a small remnant remaining after destruction.
medium.q: Why did the people say they were “left but a few of many”?

answers: Who would be king of Judah
The way wherein they might walk and the thing they should do
When the next battle would begin
medium.explanation: They asked to know the way they should follow and the action they should take.
medium.q: What did the people ask the Lord to show them?

answers: The people who remained
The people who disappeared
The people born in Egypt
medium.explanation: A remnant is a group left after others have been lost or removed.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “remnant” mean?

answers: The people claimed they were willing to accept God's word even if it was difficult
The people did not want to hear God's answer
The people had already decided to go into Egypt
challenge.explanation: They declared that they would accept the Lord's answer regardless of whether it pleased them.
challenge.q: What does the promise to obey “whether it be good, or whether it be evil” reveal?

answers: They wanted divine guidance after a difficult situation
They wanted him to appoint a king
They wanted him to cancel the law
challenge.explanation: The remnant needed to know how to act after the destruction and crisis.
challenge.q: Why did the people ask Jeremiah to pray for them?

answers: They asked the Lord to be a true and faithful witness
They refused to listen to Jeremiah
They asked that God's answer be hidden
challenge.explanation: They called the Lord a true and faithful witness and promised to do what He said.
challenge.q: What makes the people's request sound like a serious commitment?

paragraphs.title: God's Answer: Remaining in the Land and Protection from the King of Babylon

answers: Three days
Ten days
Forty days
easy.explanation: The passage says that the word of the Lord came after ten days.
easy.q: How long was it before the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah?

answers: Remain in it
Leave it immediately
Go to the king of Babylon
easy.explanation: The Lord said that if they continued to abide in the land, He would build and plant them.
easy.q: What did the Lord tell the people to do concerning the land?

answers: The king of Babylon
Jeremiah
Their own people
easy.explanation: The Lord specifically told them not to be afraid of the king of Babylon.
easy.q: Whom did the Lord tell the people not to fear?

answers: Build and plant them
Send them into exile and war
Bring famine and pestilence upon them
medium.explanation: The Lord promised, “I will build you, and not pull you down, and I will plant you, and not pluck you up.”
medium.q: What did the Lord promise to do for the remnant if it stayed in the land?

answers: The Lord would be with them to save and deliver them
The king of Babylon would leave willingly
The people had a larger army
medium.explanation: The Lord promised to be with them and deliver them from the king's hand.
medium.q: Why did the people not need to fear the king of Babylon?

answers: The Lord would establish them in the land rather than remove them
The Lord would send them to another country
The Lord would cause them to leave the land
medium.explanation: The image of planting describes stability and continued residence in the land.
medium.q: What does “I will plant you, and not pluck you up” mean in context?

answers: The people feared the king of Babylon, but the Lord promised to deliver them
The people wanted to remain in the land, but the Lord commanded them to leave
The people asked for war, but the Lord promised famine
challenge.explanation: Although the people feared Babylon's king, the Lord promised to be with them and save them.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the Lord's message?

answers: The people could be restored and established in their own land
The people would be forced to go into Egypt
The people would lose all hope
challenge.explanation: The Lord promised mercy and said He would cause them to return to their own land.
challenge.q: What does the Lord's promise to show mercy suggest about staying in the land?

answers: The Lord expresses a change in His announced judgment toward them
The Lord announces that the punishment will immediately increase
The Lord commands them to punish others
challenge.explanation: The Lord presents the possibility of restoration instead of continuing the destruction He had brought upon them.
challenge.q: What does “I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you” mean in this context?

paragraphs.title: The Warning Against Going Down to Egypt

answers: Egypt
Babylon
Another land within Judah
easy.explanation: They considered going into the land of Egypt to dwell there.
easy.q: Into which land did the people consider going?

answers: War, the sound of the trumpet, and hunger
Building and planting
Prayer and prophecy
easy.explanation: They expected Egypt to be a place where they would see no war, hear no trumpet, and have no hunger.
easy.q: What did the people hope to avoid in Egypt?

answers: The sword and famine
Peace and prosperity
Building and planting
easy.explanation: The Lord warned that the sword and famine they feared would overtake them in Egypt.
easy.q: What would overtake the people in Egypt according to the Lord?

answers: The people refused to remain in the land and obey the Lord's voice
Egypt was too near Judah
The people had already returned to the land
medium.explanation: Their error was refusing to dwell in the land and obey the Lord as instructed.
medium.q: Why was going into Egypt wrong according to the Lord's message?

answers: The sword, famine, and pestilence
Rain, peace, and blessing
Building, planting, and mercy
medium.explanation: The passage says they would die by the sword, famine, and pestilence.
medium.q: Which judgments are named for those who go into Egypt?

answers: They would not see the place from which they came
They would immediately return to Judah
They would receive protection from Babylon

medium.q: What would happen to those who went into Egypt to dwell there?

answers: The dangers the people wanted to escape would overtake them in Egypt
The people feared Egypt, but the Lord sent them there
The people wanted to stay in the land, and the dangers disappeared
challenge.explanation: They sought to avoid war and famine, but those very dangers would reach them in Egypt.
challenge.q: What is the ironic reversal in Jeremiah's warning?

answers: The people set their faces to enter Egypt and sojourn there
The people remained in the land and rebuilt it
The people asked Jeremiah to pray again
challenge.explanation: The warning applies if the people choose to leave the land and dwell in Egypt.
challenge.q: What condition introduces the warning about Egypt?

answers: None of them would remain or escape from the evil
They would receive mercy and return to the land
They would be rescued from the king of Babylon
challenge.explanation: The passage says that none of them would remain or escape from the evil brought upon them.
challenge.q: How severe would the result be for those who went into Egypt?

answers: Do not go into Egypt
Build a temple in Egypt
Fight against Judah

They had saved themselves
They had built themselves up

answers: The sword, famine, and pestilence

medium.q: In context, what does “ye dissembled in your hearts” mean?

answers: To show that they had promised beforehand to obey the Lord's answer
To say that he had not prayed at all
To announce that the Lord had not answered
medium.explanation: He highlights the difference between their promise to obey and their actual disobedience.
medium.q: Why does Jeremiah remind them that they sent him to pray?

answers: They had apparently decided to go into Egypt before hearing the answer
They did not know that Egypt existed
They wanted to remain in the land at any cost

challenge.q: What is Jeremiah's main accusation against the people?

answers: The message was given clearly and at that present time
The message would be given only in the future
The message no longer applied to them
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah stresses that he had plainly delivered the Lord's message to them that day.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “I have this day declared it to you” emphasize?

answers: Their promise to obey the Lord is shown to be disobedience
Their promise is fulfilled by their going into Egypt
The request and the ending are unrelated
